content.title: About
content.content: Angel food cake is a light, airy dessert made from egg whites, sugar, and flour. It has a delicate flavor and virtually no fat, making it a popular choice for low‑calorie desserts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name comes from the cake’s fluffy, “angelic” texture.
Traditionally it is made without yolks, which gives it a more porous crumb.
In the United States it is often used as a base for fruit tarts and mousses.
A cream‑of‑tartar or acid is added to stabilize egg whites and achieve maximum rise.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Because only egg whites are used, the cake contains very little saturated fat, which is heart‑friendly.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Egg whites provide a complete source of protein essential for tissue repair.

items.title: Moderate glycemic impact
items.content: When consumed in reasonable portions, angel food cake raises blood sugar more gently than richer, butter‑laden cakes.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: The cake contains egg whites, which can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Typical recipes use a fair amount of sugar, which may be problematic for diabetics.

items.title: Fragile texture
items.content: Angel food cake is delicate and can crumble easily, so it should be sliced and handled gently.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the cake with berry coulis, fresh fruit, a light whipped topping, or simply dusted with powdered sugar. It is also commonly used as a layer in multi‑tiered desserts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the finished cake in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer storage, refrigerate for up to 5 days or freeze for up to 2 months.
